sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ samāsādya sāmātyaṃ bharatarṣabha duḥkhārto bharataśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Approaching Duryodhana along with his ministers, O bull of the Bhāratas, Duḥśāsana, tormented by grief, O foremost of the Bhāratas, spoke these words.

sanskrit: duḥkhenaitat samānītaṃ sthaviro nāśayaty asau śatrusād gamayad dravyaṃ tad budhyadhvaṃ mahārathāḥ
english: "That which was gathered with such difficulty, the old man is now destroying; he is handing over our wealth to our enemies — understand this, O great warriors!"

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ mithaḥ saṃgamya sahitāḥ pāṇḍavān prati māninaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala, proud in their enmity toward the Pāṇḍavas, came together in private counsel,

sanskrit: vaicitravīryaṃ rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam abhigamya tvarāyuktāḥ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: and hastening to the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vicitravīrya, they spoke these smooth words:

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca na tvayedaṃ śrutaṃ rājan yaj jagāda bṛhaspatiḥ śakrasya nītiṃ pravadan vidvān devapurohitaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "Have you not heard, O king, what the wise Bṛhaspati, preceptor of the gods, declared when expounding statecraft to Indra?

sanskrit: sarvopāyair nihantavyāḥ śatravaḥ śatrukarṣaṇa purā yuddhād balād vāpi prakurvanti tavāhitam
english: Enemies must be destroyed by every means, O crusher of foes, before they do harm — before battle, before open force.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pāṇḍavadhanaiḥ sarvān saṃpūjya pārthivān yadi tān yodhayiṣyāmaḥ kiṃ vā naḥ parihāsyati
english: If the Pāṇḍavas, using their wealth, honor all the kings and then fight us, what will remain of us to escape their reach?

sanskrit: ahīn āśīviṣān kruddhān daṃśāya samupasthitān kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca pṛṣṭhe ca kaḥ samutsraṣṭum arhati
english: Who would be right to release enraged venomous serpents that have come ready to bite, after placing them around his neck and back?

sanskrit: āttaśastrā rathagatāḥ kupitās tāta pāṇḍavāḥ niḥśeṣaṃ naḥ kariṣyanti kruddhā hy āśīviṣā yathā
english: The Pāṇḍavas, O father, armed and mounted on their chariots in anger, will annihilate us completely — for the enraged are like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: saṃnaddho hy arjuno yāti vivṛtya parameṣudhī gāṇḍīvaṃ muhur ādatte niḥśvasaṃś ca nirīkṣate
english: Arjuna departs fully armored, having uncovered his great quiver, taking up the Gāṇḍīva bow again and again, breathing heavily and looking around.

sanskrit: gadāṃ gurvīṃ samudyamya tvaritaś ca vṛkodaraḥ svarathaṃ yojayitvāśu niryāta iti naḥ śrutam
english: And Vṛkodara, raising his massive mace in haste, quickly yoked his chariot and departed — so we have heard.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ khaḍgam ādāya carma cāpy aṣṭacandrakam sahadevaś ca rājā ca cakrur ākāram iṅgitaiḥ
english: Nakula took up his sword and his shield adorned with eight moons; and Sahadeva and the king too showed their intentions by their gestures.

sanskrit: te tv āsthāya rathān sarve bahuśastraparicchadān abhighnanto rathavrātān senāyogāya niryayuḥ
english: All of them, mounting their chariots laden with many weapons, shaking the masses of vehicles, set out for the marshaling of the army.

sanskrit: na kṣaṃsyante tathāsmābhir jātu viprakṛtā hi te draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ kas teṣāṃ kṣantum arhati
english: Those who have been so wronged by us will never forgive — and who among them could forgive the humiliation of Draupadī?

sanskrit: punar dīvyāma bhadraṃ te vanavāsāya pāṇḍavaiḥ evam etān vaśe kartuṃ śakṣyāmo bharatarṣabha
english: Let us gamble again — good fortune to you — with the Pāṇḍavas for the stake of forest exile; in this way we shall be able to bring them under our power, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: te vā dvādaśa varṣāṇi vayaṃ vā dyūtanirjitāḥ praviśema mahāraṇyam ajinaiḥ prativāsitāḥ
english: Either they, or we if defeated at dice, shall enter the great forest clad in the hides of deer.

sanskrit: trayodaśaṃ ca sajane ajñātāḥ parivatsaram jñātāś ca punar anyāni vane varṣāṇi dvādaśa
english: And the thirteenth year they must spend unrecognized among people; if recognized, another twelve years in the forest.

sanskrit: nivasema vayaṃ te vā tathā dyūtaṃ pravartatām akṣān uptvā punardyūtam idaṃ dīvyantu pāṇḍavāḥ
english: So shall we or they dwell; let the game proceed thus — let the Pāṇḍavas throw the dice and play this second gambling match.

sanskrit: etat kṛtyatamaṃ rājann asmākaṃ bharatarṣabha ayaṃ hi śakunir veda savidyām akṣasaṃpadam
english: This is the most necessary action for us, O king, O bull of the Bhāratas; for Śakuni here knows the science and skill of dice.

sanskrit: dṛḍhamūlā vayaṃ rājye mitrāṇi parigṛhya ca sāravad vipulaṃ sainyaṃ satkṛtya ca durāsadam
english: We are firmly rooted in the kingdom, having gathered allies and honored a vast and formidable army of worth.

sanskrit: te ca trayodaśe varṣe pārayiṣyanti ced vratam jeṣyāmas tān vayaṃ rājan rocatāṃ te paraṃtapa
english: And if they fulfill their vow in the thirteenth year, we shall still defeat them, O king — let this please you, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tūrṇaṃ pratyānayasvaitān kāmaṃ vyadhvagatān api āgacchantu punardyūtam idaṃ kurvantu pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Bring them back quickly, even though they have already set out on the road. Let them come back and let the Pāṇḍavas play this second game of dice."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato droṇaḥ somadatto bāhlīkaś ca mahārathaḥ viduro droṇaputraś ca vaiśyāputraś ca vīryavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Droṇa, Somadatta, the great warrior Bāhlika, Vidura, Droṇa's son, and the valiant son of Vaiśya —

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śāṃtanavo vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ mā dyūtam ity abhāṣanta śamo 'stv iti ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, the son of Śaṃtanu, and the great warrior Vikarṇa — all of them said "No gambling!" and "Let there be peace!" in every way.

sanskrit: akāmānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ suhṛdām arthadarśinām akarot pāṇḍavāhvānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ sutapriyaḥ
english: But Dhṛtarāṣṭra, devoted to his son, issued the summons to the Pāṇḍavas even against the will of all his well-wishers who could see what was truly beneficial.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram putrahārdād dharmayuktaṃ gāndhārī śokakarśitā
english: Then Gāndhārī, wasted by grief, spoke righteously to the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, whose heart was swayed by love for his son:

sanskrit: jāte duryodhane kṣattā mahāmatir abhāṣata nīyatāṃ paralokāya sādhv ayaṃ kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: "When Duryodhana was born, the great-minded Vidura declared: 'This one, the defiler of the family, should rightly be sent to the other world.'

sanskrit: vyanadaj jātamātro hi gomāyur iva bhārata anto nūnaṃ kulasyāsya kuravas tan nibodhata
english: For he cried out like a jackal the very moment he was born, O Bhārata — truly this is the end of this family; understand that, O Kurus.

sanskrit: mā bālānām aśiṣṭānām abhimaṃsthā matiṃ prabho mā kulasya kṣaye ghore kāraṇaṃ tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: O lord, do not follow the counsel of these foolish and ill-bred boys; do not yourself become the cause of this terrible destruction of the family.

sanskrit: baddhaṃ setuṃ ko nu bhindyād dhamec chāntaṃ ca pāvakam śame dhṛtān punaḥ pārthān kopayet ko nu bhārata
english: Who would demolish a built dam? Who would blow upon a fire that is extinguished? Who, O Bhārata, would provoke the Pārthas who have been held in check by peace?

sanskrit: smarantaṃ tvām ājamīḍha smārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ śāstraṃ na śāsti durbuddhiṃ śreyase vetarāya vā
english: O Ajamīḍha, I remind you now as you yourself remember: scripture does not rule over the evil-minded — for their good or otherwise.

sanskrit: na vai vṛddho bālamatir bhaved rājan kathaṃ cana tvannetrāḥ santu te putrā mā tvāṃ dīrṇāḥ prahāsiṣuḥ
english: Surely the old should never have a childish mind, O king. Let your sons be guided by your eyes — let them not split apart and mock you.

sanskrit: śamena dharmeṇa parasya buddhyā; jātā buddhiḥ sāstu te mā pratīpā pradhvaṃsinī krūrasamāhitā śrīr; mṛduprauḍhā gacchati putrapautrān
english: May the understanding born of peace, righteousness, and another's wisdom prevail in you — not the contrary, destructive kind; for prosperity, firm yet gentle, passes on to sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahārājo gāndhārīṃ dharmadarśinīm antaḥ kāmaṃ kulasyāstu na śakṣyāmi nivāritum
english: Then the great king replied to Gāndhārī who saw righteously: "Though my heart desires the good of the family, I am unable to restrain this.

sanskrit: yathecchanti tathaivāstu pratyāgacchantu pāṇḍavāḥ punardyūtaṃ prakurvantu māmakāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Let it be as they wish. Let the Pāṇḍavas come back; let my sons play the second gambling match together with the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vyadhvagataṃ pārthaṃ prātikāmī yudhiṣṭhiram uvāca vacanād rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the messenger Pratikamin addressed Yudhiṣṭhira the Pārtha, who had already set out on the road, conveying the words of the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra:

sanskrit: upastīrṇā sabhā rājann akṣān uptvā yudhiṣṭhira ehi pāṇḍava dīvyeti pitā tvām āha bhārata
english: "The assembly hall is prepared, O king. After the dice have been cast, come, O Pāṇḍava — your father calls you to play, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhātur niyogād bhūtāni prāpnuvanti śubhāśubham na nivṛttis tayor asti devitavyaṃ punar yadi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "By the command of the Creator, beings receive their good and evil — there is no escape from either; if I must play again —

sanskrit: akṣadyūte samāhvānaṃ niyogāt sthavirasya ca jānann api kṣayakaraṃ nātikramitum utsahe
english: — a summons to dice-play, and by the command of the elder — knowing even that it leads to ruin, I do not dare to transgress it."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca iti bruvan nivavṛte bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaḥ jānaṃś ca śakuner māyāṃ pārtho dyūtam iyāt punaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Speaking thus, the Pāṇḍava turned back with his brothers; though knowing the deceit of Śakuni, the Pārtha went again to the gambling match.

sanskrit: viviśus te sabhāṃ tāṃ tu punar eva mahārathāḥ vyathayanti sma cetāṃsi suhṛdāṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Those great warriors, bulls of the Bhāratas, entered that assembly hall once again, distressing the hearts of their well-wishers.

sanskrit: yathopajoṣam āsīnāḥ punardyūtapravṛttaye sarvalokavināśāya daivenopanipīḍitāḥ
english: They sat down as they pleased, pressed onward by fate, for the conduct of a second gambling match — and for the destruction of all the world.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca amuñcat sthaviro yad vo dhanaṃ pūjitam eva tat mahādhanaṃ glahaṃ tv ekaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha
english: Śakuni said: "The old man has released the wealth that was already won — it remains honored. But now hear this one great stake from me, O bull of the Bhāratas:

sanskrit: vayaṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi yuṣmābhir dyūtanirjitāḥ praviśema mahāraṇyaṃ rauravājinavāsasaḥ
english: We, defeated by you at dice, shall enter the great forest for twelve years, clad in the hides of the ruru deer —

sanskrit: trayodaśaṃ ca sajane ajñātāḥ parivatsaram jñātāś ca punar anyāni vane varṣāṇi dvādaśa
english: and the thirteenth year we shall spend unrecognized among people; if recognized, another twelve years in the forest.

sanskrit: asmābhir vā jitā yūyaṃ vane varṣāṇi dvādaśa vasadhvaṃ kṛṣṇayā sārdham ajinaiḥ prativāsitāḥ
english: Or if you are conquered by us, you shall dwell in the forest for twelve years, together with Kṛṣṇā, clad in deerskins.

sanskrit: trayodaśe ca nirvṛtte punar eva yathocitam svarājyaṃ pratipattavyam itarair atha vetaraiḥ
english: And when the thirteenth year has passed, the proper kingdom is to be reclaimed — by one side or the other.

sanskrit: anena vyavasāyena sahāsmābhir yudhiṣṭhira akṣān uptvā punardyūtam ehi dīvyasva bhārata
english: With this as the agreed stake, come, Yudhiṣṭhira — throw the dice with us in this second gambling match, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: sabhāsada ūcuḥ aho dhig bāndhavā nainaṃ bodhayanti mahad bhayam buddhyā bodhyaṃ na budhyante svayaṃ ca bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: The spectators in the assembly said: "Alas, shame! His kinsmen do not warn him of this great danger; and the bulls of the Bhāratas themselves do not grasp with their own understanding what should be grasped by understanding."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca janapravādān subahūn iti śṛṇvan narādhipaḥ hriyā ca dharmasaṅgāc ca pārtho dyūtam iyāt punaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing these many murmurs of the people, the lord of men — from a sense of honor and from adherence to dharma — the Pārtha went again to the gambling match.

sanskrit: jānann api mahābuddhiḥ punardyūtam avartayat apy ayaṃ na vināśaḥ syāt kurūṇām iti cintayan
english: Even knowing, the greatly intelligent one set the second game in motion, thinking: "Perhaps this will not be the destruction of the Kurus after all."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ vai madvidho rājā svadharmam anupālayan āhūto vinivarteta dīvyāmi śakune tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "How could a king like me, maintaining his own duty, turn back once summoned? I will play against you, O Śakuni."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca gavāśvaṃ bahudhenūkam aparyantam ajāvikam gajāḥ kośo hiraṇyaṃ ca dāsīdāsaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Śakuni said: "Cattle and horses, many milk-cows beyond counting, goats and sheep, elephants, treasure, gold, and all male and female slaves —

sanskrit: eṣa no glaha evaiko vanavāsāya pāṇḍavāḥ yūyaṃ vayaṃ vā vijitā vasema vanam āśritāḥ
english: this is our one single stake — forest exile for the Pāṇḍavas: either you or we, whichever is defeated, shall take refuge in the forest."

sanskrit: anena vyavasāyena dīvyāma bharatarṣabha samutkṣepeṇa caikena vanavāsāya bhārata
english: "With this resolve, let us play, O bull of the Bhāratas — with a single throw, for the stake of forest exile, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratijagrāha taṃ pārtho glahaṃ jagrāha saubalaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The Pārtha accepted the stake; the son of Subala threw the dice. "Won!" — thus Śakuni declared to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vanavāsāya cakrus te matiṃ pārthāḥ parājitāḥ ajināny uttarīyāṇi jagṛhuś ca yathākramam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Defeated, the Pārthas resolved themselves to forest exile and took up their deerskins as upper garments, one by one in order.

sanskrit: ajinaiḥ saṃvṛtān dṛṣṭvā hṛtarājyān ariṃdamān prasthitān vanavāsāya tato duḥśāsano 'bravīt
english: Seeing those subduer-of-foes clad in deerskins, their kingdom seized, setting out for forest exile, Duḥśāsana then spoke:

sanskrit: pravṛttaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya cakraṃ rājño mahātmanaḥ parābhūtāḥ pāṇḍuputrā vipattiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
english: "The wheel of the great-souled king, son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, has rolled forward; the sons of Pāṇḍu are defeated and have fallen into supreme misfortune.

sanskrit: adya devāḥ saṃprayātāḥ samair vartmabhir asthalaiḥ guṇajyeṣṭhās tathā jyeṣṭhā bhūyāṃso yad vayaṃ paraiḥ
english: Today the gods have departed by level paths, without obstacles; even those eldest in virtue, those elders — yet we are greater than our opponents.

sanskrit: narakaṃ pātitāḥ pārthā dīrghakālam anantakam sukhāc ca hīnā rājyāc ca vinaṣṭāḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ
english: The Pārthas have been cast into hell for a long and endless time; deprived of happiness and kingdom, they are ruined for eternal years.

sanskrit: balena mattā ye te sma dhārtarāṣṭrān prahāsiṣuḥ te nirjitā hṛtadhanā vanam eṣyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Those who, intoxicated by strength, used to mock the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — those Pāṇḍavas, now defeated and their wealth seized, shall go to the forest.

sanskrit: citrān saṃnāhān avamuñcantu caiṣāṃ; vāsāṃsi divyāni ca bhānumanti nivāsyantāṃ rurucarmāṇi sarve; yathā glahaṃ saubalasyābhyupetāḥ
english: "Let them remove their colorful armor and their resplendent divine garments; let them all now put on ruru-deer hides — as they agreed to the stake of Subala's son."

sanskrit: na santi lokeṣu pumāṃsa īdṛśā; ity eva ye bhāvitabuddhayaḥ sadā jñāsyanti te ''tmānam ime 'dya pāṇḍavā; viparyaye ṣaṇḍhatilā ivāphalāḥ
english: "Those who were always of the conviction that 'there are no men in the world like these' — those Pāṇḍavas will today know themselves in this reversal, like barren sesame plants bearing no fruit."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi vāsodaya īdṛśānāṃ; manasvināṃ kaurava mā bhaved vaḥ adīkṣitānām ajināni yadvad; balīyasāṃ paśyata pāṇḍavānām
english: "For this is the fitting attire of such proud men, O Kaurava — may it not fall to us! Look at the Pāṇḍavas, those mighty ones, now like the uninitiated wearing deerskins."

sanskrit: mahāprājñaḥ somako yajñasenaḥ; kanyāṃ pāñcālīṃ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ pradāya akārṣīd vai duṣkṛtaṃ neha santi; klībāḥ pārthāḥ patayo yājñasenyāḥ
english: "The greatly wise Somaka Yajñasena did an evil deed by giving the Pāñcālī maiden to the Pāṇḍavas; for the Pārthas, husbands of Yājñasenī, are no more — they are as eunuchs now."

sanskrit: sūkṣmān prāvārān ajināni coditān; dṛṣṭvāraṇye nirdhanān apratiṣṭhān kāṃ tvaṃ prītiṃ lapsyase yājñaseni; patiṃ vṛṇīṣva yam ihānyam icchasi
english: "Having seen these fine garments exchanged for deerskins, your husbands in the forest destitute and without standing — what joy will you find, O Yājñasenī? Choose another husband here whom you desire."

sanskrit: ete hi sarve kuravaḥ sametāḥ; kṣāntā dāntāḥ sudraviṇopapannāḥ eṣāṃ vṛṇīṣvaikatamaṃ patitve; na tvāṃ tapet kālaviparyayo 'yam
english: "All the Kurus assembled here are patient, self-controlled, and richly endowed with wealth. Choose one among them as a husband — this reversal of fortune need not burn you."

sanskrit: yathāphalāḥ ṣaṇḍhatilā yathā carmamayā mṛgāḥ tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve yathā kākayavā api
english: "Like barren sesame plants bearing no fruit, like deer made of leather, like black barley — just so are all the Pāṇḍavas now."

sanskrit: kiṃ pāṇḍavāṃs tvaṃ patitān upāsse; moghaḥ śramaḥ ṣaṇḍhatilān upāsya evaṃ nṛśaṃsaḥ paruṣāṇi pārthān; aśrāvayad dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ
english: "Why do you wait upon these fallen Pāṇḍavas? Service to barren sesame is wasted effort." Thus the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, cruel and harsh, made the Pārthas hear these words.

sanskrit: tad vai śrutvā bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣī; nirbhartsyoccais taṃ nigṛhyaiva roṣāt uvācedaṃ sahasaivopagamya; siṃho yathā haimavataḥ śṛgālam
english: Hearing that, Bhīmasena, deeply furious, stepped forward suddenly, rebuked him loudly, seized him in his rage, and spoke these words — like a Himālayan lion to a jackal:

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca krūra pāpajanair juṣṭam akṛtārthaṃ prabhāṣase gāndhāravidyayā hi tvaṃ rājamadhye vikatthase
english: Bhīmasena said: "O cruel one, you speak what is fitting only for the wicked, for those who have accomplished nothing; it is by the dice-skill of Gāndhāra that you boast in the midst of kings.

sanskrit: yathā tudasi marmāṇi vākśarair iha no bhṛśam tathā smārayitā te 'haṃ kṛntan marmāṇi saṃyuge
english: Even as you pierce our vital points deeply here with word-arrows, so shall I remind you of it, cutting your vital points in battle.

sanskrit: ye ca tvām anuvartante kāmalobhavaśānugāḥ goptāraḥ sānubandhāṃs tān neṣyāmi yamasādanam
english: And those who follow you, enslaved by desire and greed — those protectors along with their kin — I shall drive to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvāṇam ajinair vivāsitaṃ; duḥkhābhibhūtaṃ parinṛtyati sma madhye kurūṇāṃ dharmanibaddhamārgaṃ; gaur gaur iti smāhvayan muktalajjaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While Bhīma was speaking thus, clad in deerskins, overwhelmed with grief — bound to the path of dharma — Duḥśāsana danced around him in the midst of the Kurus, calling out "Cow! Cow!" utterly without shame.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca nṛśaṃsaṃ paruṣaṃ krūraṃ śakyaṃ duḥśāsana tvayā nikṛtyā hi dhanaṃ labdhvā ko vikatthitum arhati
english: Bhīmasena said: "What is cruel, harsh, and vicious — that indeed you are capable of, O Duḥśāsana. Having gained wealth by fraud, who deserves to boast?

sanskrit: mā ha sma sukṛtāṃl lokān gacchet pārtho vṛkodaraḥ yadi vakṣasi bhittvā te na pibec choṇitaṃ raṇe
english: May the Pārtha Vṛkodara never attain the worlds of those who have done good deeds, if he does not drink your blood in battle after splitting open your chest."

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrān raṇe hatvā miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām śamaṃ gantāsmi nacirāt satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ
english: "Having slain the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in battle before the eyes of all the archers, I shall soon attain peace — this truth I declare to you."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya rājā siṃhagateḥ sakhelaṃ; duryodhano bhīmasenasya harṣāt gatiṃ svagatyānucakāra mando; nirgacchatāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ sabhāyāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As Bhīmasena moved with his lion-stride, king Duryodhana, that dull-witted one, joyfully mimicked Bhīmasena's gait with his own gait, as the Pāṇḍavas were leaving the assembly hall.

sanskrit: naitāvatā kṛtam ity abravīt taṃ; vṛkodaraḥ saṃnivṛttārdhakāyaḥ śīghraṃ hi tvā nihataṃ sānubandhaṃ; saṃsmāryāhaṃ prativakṣyāmi mūḍha
english: Vṛkodara, turning back halfway, said to him: "This is not done with yet — I shall swiftly remind you of it after slaying you together with your kin, O fool."
